title: Knowledge-Centric Automated Issue Resolution: A Systematic Survey and Taxonomy
comment: 91 pages, 22 figures
summary: Automated issue resolution is a knowledge-intensive software maintenance task in which LLM-based agents must acquire, represent, use, and update knowledge from repositories, execution environments, historical artifacts, documents, tools, and prior repair processes. title: Loop Engineering: Version-Bound, Evidence-Gated Coordination for Production Coding Agents
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Sanitized supporting data included in the source package. Zenodo preprint DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21504929

title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood

summary: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. title: AI Cannot Review What Humans Catch: A First Look at the Reviews of Agent Instruction Files

title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
summary: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases. An authorization analysis further shows that identical visible transcripts can require different safety decisions depending on the governing policy, a distinction no observation-only classifier can resolve. These results argue for behavioral and policy-grounded evaluation over text-similarity guardrails.

title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
comment: 28 pages, 7 figures. Code and leaderboard: https://github.com/Btwestyo/sciresearch-eval
summary: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. Fable 5.2 is the most accurate model at default effort (interval score 1.9 times better than Astra's) but writes 6 times as many tokens, and at Astra's token count it falls short. We release the environment, graders and harness.
